summary: Security and BCDR-focused review for potential Redwood deployment at Zenwell Health. Discussed SOC 2 / ISO posture, RBAC/SSO options, audit logs and retention, encryption and KMS options incl customer-managed keys, incident response runbook, RTO/RPO targets, uptime SLA and escalation process. Agreed next steps to share docs and runbook walkthrough and align on contract SLA language.
transcript:
[00:00] Arielle Gomez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we scheduled 50 minutes for this. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Marcus Lee: Marcus Lee, CISO at Zenwell.
[00:07] Priya Nair: Priya, Head of SRE.
[00:09] Ethan Browne: Ethan, procurement.
[00:10] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia, compliance.
[00:12] Samir Patel: Samir from Redwood SE.
[00:14] Arielle Gomez: Great, cool. Objective for today is to go through incident response, BCDR, SLA/uptime, and escalation — and make sure our security posture maps to Zenwell's requirements.
[00:25] Marcus Lee: Sounds good. I skimmed the security package you sent, couple questions about the incident response timelines and how your RTO/RPO looks across hosted vs dedicated.
[00:34] Samir Patel: Yeah, good point. So we treat hosted and dedicated a bit differently. For hosted, our standard customer-facing SLA is 99.9% with an operational playbook that assumes multi-region failover for critical tenants. For Dedicated, because you have reserved capacity we can support tighter RTOs depending on topology. Our runbook defines the typical steps and estimated RTOs — but there are variables like model warm-up and KV cache rebuild.
[00:55] Priya Nair: When you say KV cache rebuild, what's the typical warm-up? For our inference-critical endpoints we need sub-200ms p95 latency and can't wait 30 minutes for cache warming.
[01:05] Samir Patel: Right. So warm-up is highly workload dependent. For small models and with preloaded prefixes you can see cache priming in a few minutes, for larger LLMs the KV restore across shards can take longer. For Dedicated we offer snapshotting for KV caches and pre-warming during failover to reduce RTO — that was one of the main features we designed for enterprise BCDR.
[01:28] Marcus Lee: Do you have concrete RTO/RPO numbers in a runbook we can use in our SOW?
[01:33] Samir Patel: We do. I'll share the RTO/RPO matrix excerpt. Typical published ranges are: RTO 5-30 minutes for control-plane failover, 30-90 minutes for full KV cache rebuild without snapshot, and RPO is near-zero for control plane (since we replicate metadata) but for ephemeral session state it depends on persistence settings. I'll attach the exact table.
[01:54] Sofia Alvarez: On the compliance side I need to confirm audit log retention. What's your default retention for audit logs and can we route logs to customer SPLUNK or S3 for long-term retention?
[02:03] Samir Patel: Audit logs are retained in our control plane for 180 days by default. We can export to customer-managed S3 buckets or SIEM via syslog/HTTPS. For Private deployments we can do longer retention per contract.
[02:17] Priya Nair: We will need at least 1 year of immutable audit logs for certain workloads. Is that doable?
[02:20] Arielle Gomez: Yes, that's a common ask. For Hosted we typically push exports to customer S3 with lifecycle policies that Zenwell manages. For Dedicated/Private we can add contractual retention clauses and WORM settings if required.
[02:33] Marcus Lee: Encryption — we want customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM-backed KMS. Do you support BYOK with HSM?
[02:40] Samir Patel: We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or external HSM integrations for Private deployments. For Hosted we support CMKs in supported cloud regions (the key material can be customer controlled via AWS KMS). Full on-prem HSM + BYOK is part of our Private offering.
[02:54] Marcus Lee: And what about data in flight and at rest? TLS 1.2+, and AES-256 for at-rest?
[02:59] Samir Patel: Yep TLS 1.2+ and TLS 1.3 for in flight, and AES-256 for data at rest. Key rotation policies are supported — we log key usage in audit logs.
[03:09] Priya Nair: Great. Let's shift to incident response — how does Redwood handle detection, triage, escalation? Walk me through a P1 incident.
[03:16] Lena Ortiz: I'll take that. For a P1 — severe outage or data breach — our on-call runs a triage within 15 minutes, assemble the incident commander and critical engineers. We use an internal pager and also have a customer-facing incident status page. Escalation tiers: Tier 1 on-call SE, Tier 2 engineering owners, Tier 3 product and leadership. For enterprise customers we map a direct escalation path and provide a named CSM/SE contact.
[03:41] Marcus Lee: Is there a guaranteed initial response SLA and communication cadence?
[03:45] Lena Ortiz: We commit to acknowledging within 15 minutes for Sev1, status updates at 30/60 minutes and then hourly unless otherwise agreed. The exact cadence can be adjusted in the SLA appendix.
[03:56] Priya Nair: And post-incident, do you provide postmortem with root cause analysis and remediation timelines?
[04:01] Samir Patel: Yes. For Sev1 we provide a preliminary incident report within 48 hours and a full RCA in 10 business days typically. We can accommodate tighter timelines by contract.
[04:12] Marcus Lee: On the security front, SOC 2 — do you have a current Type II? Does Redwood undergo ISO 27001?
[04:18] Arielle Gomez: We have SOC 2 Type II, most recent audit completed Q4 2024. We're currently in progress on ISO 27001 certification and expect completion mid-2025. We'll share the SOC2 snapshot and the pen test summary after the call.
[04:32] Sofia Alvarez: Are the SOC 2 logs available for review as part of our security assessment?
[04:36] Arielle Gomez: We can provide the SOC reports under NDA and a security package with evidence. We can't release raw logs, but we can provide redacted supporting artifacts and evidence.
[04:46] Ethan Browne: Procurement question: SLA credits — how are they calculated and is there a max credit for downtime?
[04:52] Samir Patel: Our default SLA credit model is percentage-of-monthly-service fee pro-rated by the downtime window. For critical enterprise contracts we negotiate a tailored credit cap and service credit ladder.
[05:02] Ethan Browne: We typically push for a higher uptime (99.95%) or deeper credits. Is that feasible?
[05:07] Arielle Gomez: We can discuss 99.95 for Dedicated with contractual commitments and resilience patterns. The price and reserved capacity would reflect that.
[05:17] Priya Nair: What about maintenance windows and notification windows — we need at least 72 hours heads-up for planned maintenance or a slack channel notification.
[05:24] Samir Patel: Standard is 72 hours for non-critical maintenance. For urgent maintenance we notify as soon as possible; customers with Dedicated deployments can opt into maintenance blackout windows.
[05:35] Marcus Lee: Escalation process — in the case where an issue is cross-region and requires multi-team coordination, how do we get an executive escalation?
[05:43] Lena Ortiz: We have an escalation matrix that lists named contacts at each tier. Executive escalation can be triggered after the initial 60-90 minutes for unresolved Sev1 incidents, and our leadership duty officer will join. We'll include that matrix in the runbook we share.
[05:56] Priya Nair: Can we also get a mock drill / tabletop exercise? We want to validate your RTOs against our playbooks.
[06:02] Samir Patel: Absolutely — we regularly run tabletop exercises with customers. Typical session is 30-60 minutes and we can simulate failover, KV restore, and CRO scenarios. We'll coordinate a run with your SRE team.
[06:14] Marcus Lee: Regarding data residency — certain data must remain within EU. Do you have region pinning and contractual data residency guarantees?
[06:21] Samir Patel: Yes, region pinning is supported for Hosted in EU regions and for Dedicated/Private you'll have full control. We'll include region-specific deployment notes in the security package.
[06:31] Sofia Alvarez: Any third-party subprocessors we should be aware of?
[06:34] Arielle Gomez: We list major cloud providers and some managed service partners in our subprocessor list — we'll attach the current list. Any specific vendor concerns?
[06:41] Marcus Lee: Not at the moment. Two quick nitpicks: one, SLAs for model-availability (for specific model versions) — how do you handle versioned rollouts and fallback policies?
[06:50] Samir Patel: We support pinned model versions and automatic fallback to compatible variants during capacity shortage. The SLA typically measures service availability at the API level; model-level guarantees can be added for enterprise agreements.
[07:03] Priya Nair: And finally, do you provide cryptographic attestation of the runtime or reproducible build info for supply chain assurance?
[07:10] Samir Patel: We provide build manifest and signed artifacts for Private deployments. For Hosted we can provide a supply chain summary and attestations per contract terms.
[07:20] Marcus Lee: OK, that's helpful. Can you summarize next steps?
[07:23] Arielle Gomez: Sure: Samir and Lena will share the incident response runbook excerpt and RTO/RPO matrix; I'll send SOC2 and pen test report under NDA; Samir will set up a tabletop with Priya's SRE; Marcus will provide RTO/RPO targets and any data residency constraints. We'll target follow-up by 2025-05-21 to get SLA language aligned.
[07:44] Ethan Browne: I'll be looking at the SLA credit language and propose redlines.
[07:48] Marcus Lee: Thanks everyone.
[07:50] Arielle Gomez: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the links (SOC2, security package, runbook excerpt, SLA PDF).
[07:56] [END]
